A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J. The extensive reformatting and relocated pseudocode do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gridworld, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Connect4 experiments, including additional exploration comparisons in Appendix I, Figures 1–2, and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The BC procedure, LSVI-UCB-ZERO-BC, infinite-horizon extension, and DQN-Explore-BC retain their objectives and algorithmic steps. Algorithms 4–5 are relocated rather than newly introduced or modified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 3×3 Gridworld, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Connect4 tasks, plus the 5×5 Gridworld and chain Markov game in Appendix I.3.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same tabular, relational, and neural BC comparisons, and the same uniform-exploration comparator in Appendix I.3. No newly cited method is added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I retain the same feature configurations, expert generation procedures, dataset sizes, training budgets, Nash-gap evaluation, and Connect4 win-rate protocol and opponent configurations.

E4.justification: The uniform-versus-DQN exploration analysis in Gridworld and the chain environment is unchanged. Both versions also retain the Connect4 opponent analysis and the discussion of direct inversion versus Sherman–Morrison updates.

E5.justification: Appendix I retains the same seed lists and run descriptions. The shaded plot bands and tabulated ± reporting are unchanged, with no additional uncertainty estimation or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 retain identical plotted content, and Tables 1–2 retain their numerical entries. For example, Connect4 win rates against Approx. BR remain 0.21±0.04 for DQN-Explore-BC and 0.00±0.00 for BC.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.1 changes from linearity under every Markov opponent policy to linearity only after averaging over the expert opponent policy, substantially weakening the stated structural requirement. However, Appendix D.1 retains the stronger all-policy assumption; the theorem bounds and substantive proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: feature-level concentrability for BC, efficient interactive MAIL, the infinite-horizon extension, and the deep algorithm. The formal assumption revision does not introduce a separate headline contribution.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly explains that linearity is required only after averaging over the expert policy, revising the stated applicability boundary. Existing interpretations of experimental results and the limitations concerning expert realizability, concentrability estimation, and adaptive interaction remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures in Appendix I retain the same architectures, hyperparameters, expert solvers, data representations, and A100/AMD hardware information. Both PDFs provide the same code repository link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2023) and explicitly contrasts its expert-averaged linearity assumption with the broader policy requirements attributed to Cui et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2023). The extensive related-work discussion in Appendix B otherwise remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted explanatory edits, including the new assumption discussion and an explicit statement of the existing Jensen inequality step. Front matter and acknowledgements change, and a generic Impact Statement is added; the section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document into conference styling, with two-column main text and references, different typography and running headers, and reflowed appendices. Figures and tables are resized or repositioned, and Algorithms 4–5 move from the final pages beside their corresponding appendix discussions.

improvement.justification: The weaker Assumption 2.1 could broaden the theory, and relocating pseudocode improves navigation. However, Appendix D.1 still requires all-policy linearity, while Section 2.1 retains its assertion of linear Q-functions for arbitrary policy pairs. This unreconciled scope change prevents a confident assessment of the theoretical gain. With unchanged empirical evidence, the overall net quality effect remains uncertain.
